collections/combinatorics#

Lazy combinatorial iterators over finite indexed sources.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let pairs = Combinations(origin: values, size: 2);
// [a,b], [a,c], [b,c]

Description#

Lazy combinatorial iterators over finite indexed sources.

Every item is materialized only when cursor.item() is requested. The module never precomputes all results and every successor cursor is immutable. Retaining an earlier cursor therefore retains its original result.

Combinations chooses distinct positions in source order:

CombinationsWithReplacement permits a position to occur repeatedly:

let pairs = CombinationsWithReplacement(origin: values, size: 2);
// [a,a], [a,b], [a,c], [b,b], [b,c], [c,c]

Permutations emits ordered selections. Omitting size selects every source position; supplying size emits partial permutations:

let arrangements = Permutations(origin: values, size: 2);
// [a,b], [a,c], [b,a], [b,c], [c,a], [c,b]

CartesianProduct treats the outer sequence as dimensions. The rightmost dimension advances fastest.

Negative sizes throw InvalidArgument. Choosing more distinct positions than a source contains produces no results. Choosing zero positions produces one empty result. A product of zero dimensions likewise contains one empty result; a product with any empty dimension contains no results.

Laziness limits memory use, not result count. Counts grow explosively: combinations as n!/(r!(n-r)!), replacement combinations as (n+r-1)!/(r!(n-1)!), permutations as n!/(n-r)!, and products as the multiplication of all dimension sizes. Consumers should normally stop early or combine these iterators with Taken.
